title: Integral inner inverse of a finite graph incidence map
statement: Let $V,E$ be finite sets and let $s,t:E\to V$ satisfy $s(e)\ne t(e)$ for every $e\in E$. Parallel edges are permitted, and the graph need not be connected or nonempty. For a finite set $S$, write $\mathbf Z^S$ for the free $\mathbf Z$-module [def-weil-pbc-free-module] of integer-valued functions on $S$, with standard vectors $b_u$. Let $\partial:\mathbf Z^E\to\mathbf Z^V$ be the $\mathbf Z$-linear map determined by $\partial(b_e)=b_{t(e)}-b_{s(e)}$. There exists a $\mathbf Z$-linear map $r:\mathbf Z^V\to\mathbf Z^E$ such that $\partial\circ r\circ\partial=\partial$.

source.place: Agent-written integral-lattice auxiliary for Tag 0C1M, lemma-glue-points, units-sequence proof. The source motivates the edge/vertex quotient but does not assert this graph incidence splitting lemma.

proof.text: Define a relation on $V$ by $u\sim v$ if there is $c\in\mathbf Z^E$ with $\partial c=b_v-b_u$. This is an equivalence relation: $0$ witnesses $u\sim u$; if $c$ witnesses $u\sim v$, then $-c$ witnesses $v\sim u$; if $c,d$ witness $u\sim v$ and $v\sim w$, then $c+d$ witnesses $u\sim w$, since $(b_v-b_u)+(b_w-b_v)=b_w-b_u$. For every edge $e$, the vector $b_e$ witnesses $s(e)\sim t(e)$ by the defining formula for $\partial$.

source.place: Agent-written elementary integral-lattice auxiliary motivated by Tag 0C1M, lemma-glue-points, units-sequence proof; the graph argument is not asserted in that source.

proof.text: For each equivalence class $C$ choose a representative $a_C\in C$, choosing once per class. For every $v\in C$, the defining condition $a_C\sim v$ supplies a vector $p_v\in\mathbf Z^E$ with $\partial p_v=b_v-b_{a_C}$; choose one such vector. These choices use only the existential condition defining $\sim$. In particular $s(e)$ and $t(e)$ have the same chosen representative for each edge. No representatives are requested when $V$ is empty.

source.place: Agent-written elementary integral-lattice auxiliary motivated by Tag 0C1M, lemma-glue-points, units-sequence proof; the graph argument is not asserted in that source.

proof.text: Define $r:\mathbf Z^V\to\mathbf Z^E$ by the finite-sum formula $r(x)=\sum_{v\in V}x(v)p_v$. Finite distributivity gives $r(x+y)=r(x)+r(y)$ and $r(nx)=n r(x)$ for every $n\in\mathbf Z$, so this is a $\mathbf Z$-linear map. The coordinate expansion in the standard basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module] gives $r(b_v)=p_v$.

source.place: Agent-written elementary integral-lattice auxiliary motivated by Tag 0C1M, lemma-glue-points, units-sequence proof; the graph argument is not asserted in that source.

proof.text: Fix $e\in E$, and let $C$ be the common class of $s(e)$ and $t(e)$. Then $\partial r\partial(b_e)=\partial(p_{t(e)}-p_{s(e)})=(b_{t(e)}-b_{a_C})-(b_{s(e)}-b_{a_C})=b_{t(e)}-b_{s(e)}=\partial(b_e)$. For $z=\sum_{e\in E}z(e)b_e$, linearity gives $\partial r\partial(z)=\sum_e z(e)\partial r\partial(b_e)=\sum_e z(e)\partial(b_e)=\partial(z)$. The standard-basis expansion [def-weil-pbc-free-module] therefore proves $\partial\circ r\circ\partial=\partial$, including the empty sum when $E$ is empty.
